title: Optimizing Catalog Retrieval for E-commerce
business: An online retailer with a high-traffic product catalog that requires frequent database lookups for static item descriptions.
problem: Database latency spikes during peak shopping hours due to redundant queries for identical product data across multiple web server nodes.
solution: Memcached provides a distributed memory object caching system that creates a unified virtual pool of memory, allowing all web servers to retrieve frequently accessed product data from a shared cache instead of the primary database.
steps: Provision a dedicated cluster of Memcached server nodes to act as the shared memory layer.
Configure web application nodes to connect to the Memcached cluster using a consistent hashing client library.
Implement a cache-aside pattern where the application checks Memcached before querying the database.
Update the application logic to write retrieved database results into Memcached with an appropriate expiration time.
Monitor cache hit rates to ensure the distributed memory pool is effectively reducing backend database load.
outcome: Reduced database CPU utilization and faster response times for end-users as product data is served from memory.
limitation: Because Memcached is an ephemeral cache, data is not persistent; if a node fails or the cache is cleared, the application must be able to gracefully fall back to the primary database to repopulate the missing items.

questions.question: In Optimizing Catalog Retrieval for E-commerce, why is a distributed cache used?
options: To replace the database entirely for all transactions
To provide a unified virtual pool of memory to reduce database load
To ensure permanent storage of product descriptions
To increase the number of web server nodes required
questions.explanation: The scenario identifies that redundant database queries cause latency, and the solution uses a distributed cache to share memory across nodes, alleviating that specific load.
questions.evidence: Memcached provides a distributed memory object caching system that creates a unified virtual pool of memory, allowing all web servers to retrieve frequently accessed product data from a shared cache instead of the primary database.

questions.question: In Optimizing Catalog Retrieval for E-commerce, what is a primary limitation of the implementation?
options: The cache is too slow for high-traffic environments
Data is not persistent and requires a fallback mechanism
It prevents the database from ever being updated
It requires a single, non-distributed server node
questions.explanation: Memcached is ephemeral, meaning it does not store data permanently, requiring the application to handle cache misses by querying the database.
questions.evidence: Because Memcached is an ephemeral cache, data is not persistent; if a node fails or the cache is cleared, the application must be able to gracefully fall back to the primary database to repopulate the missing items.
